text: Signal HRV / RMSSD. ADHD vs neurotypical: Resting vagal HRV: no reliable difference (Koenig et al. 2017 meta-analysis). Task-related vagal HRV is reduced in children and adolescents with ADHD (Robe et al. 2019; 13 studies). One CPT study found no HR group difference but higher LF/HF. Strength/consistency: Mixed/weak. An umbrella review classed the task-related HRV reduction in ADHD as "weak evidence"; a 2026 clinical perspective notes "effect sizes are generally small and heterogeneity is substantial." Ranges: Not given as normative ADHD ranges in the sources opened; effects reported as SMDs. Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No. Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Literature frames HRV as autonomic/emotion regulation and arousal, with links to sustained attention. The 2026 clinical review explicitly ties HRV to "emotional dysregulation." Attention and emotion are not cleanly separated. Sources: Robe et al., Neurosci Biobehav Rev 2019 (sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0149763418308005); umbrella review, Transl Psychiatry 2025 (nature.com/articles/s41398-025-03339-x); Springer 2026 clinical perspective (doi 10.1186/s43045-026-00658-7); CPT-HRV study, Biol Psychol 2017 (sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0301051117300042)

Signal Electrodermal activity (EDA). ADHD vs neurotypical: Tends toward hypo-arousal (lower skin conductance level). In girls with ADHD, inattentive symptoms were predicted by reduced SCL. Lower arousal appeared only during a slow, low-demand task; it normalised under fast/incentive conditions and fluctuated more late in long sessions. Strength/consistency: Moderate but context-dependent. A 2026 systematic review declined to meta-analyse because of heterogeneity. Some adult studies show *elevated* SCRs in risk tasks. Ranges: Example: SCR threshold >0.05 μS used in a Balloon Analogue Risk Task study (n = 28 ADHD / 28 NT), where ADHD arousal stayed elevated. Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No. Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Read as sympathetic arousal. A separate literature uses EDA to index emotional reactivity/regulation in ADHD (emotion induction and suppression). The same signal therefore appears on both sides of the attention/emotion boundary. Sources: Dupuy et al. 2014 (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24125854); Psychiatry Res 2018 (sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0165178118312381); Signals 2026 review (doi 10.3390/signals7040073); emotion-regulation ANS study (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7720673)

Signal Eye tracking / gaze. ADHD vs neurotypical: Meta-analyses show more antisaccade direction errors, anticipatory errors in memory-guided saccades, and intrusive saccades during fixation. No pursuit or saccade-dysmetria deficits. Strength/consistency: Moderate–strong for oculomotor inhibition. Memory-guided saccade g = 0.86, 95% CI 0.64–1.08, I² = 17.7%. Prolonged-fixation intrusions show a large effect but high heterogeneity. Ranges: Memory-guided saccade g = 0.86. Example fixation durations (ms) in a pediatric classification study: 64.6 ± 19.7 vs 71.8 ± 16.9 (pro-saccade task). Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No. A lab-based classification study only. Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Interpreted as cognitive/inhibitory control (top-down attention). Sources: "The Eyes Have It" meta-analysis, Biol Psychiatry CNNI (sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2451902221001440); Maron et al. 2021 meta-analysis (sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0149763421004541); Frontiers Psychiatry 2024 (doi 10.3389/fpsyt.2024.1337595)

Signal Blink rate. ADHD vs neurotypical: Null in the best study. Groen et al. found no aberrant blink rate or blink modulation in unmedicated children with ADHD ("near zero effect sizes"). Caplan et al. 1996 found lower rates only during verbal recall and absent modulation across tasks. One study reported 30 vs 23 blinks/min (secondary citation, unverified). Strength/consistency: Weak / contradictory. Ranges: Groen: effect sizes near zero. Caplan: n = 28 ADHD vs 47 controls; F = 7.10, p < .008 for the verbal-recall difference. Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No. Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Framed as a proxy for central dopamine and attentional engagement. Also rises with fatigue and prolonged wakefulness (physical state). Sources: Groen et al., J Neural Transm 2017 (doi 10.1007/s00702-015-1457-6; pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5281678); Caplan et al., Biol Psychiatry 1996 (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8780838)

Signal Pupillometry. ADHD vs neurotypical: Adults with ADHD showed larger tonic (baseline) pupil and suppressed phasic (stimulus-evoked) dilation. Children show reduced phasic dilation in working-memory tasks. Strength/consistency: Moderate, few studies; no meta-analysis found. A 2026 multicentre deep-learning study (439 participants, 14 centres) used task-evoked pupil dynamics for classification. Ranges: Tonic pupil in an auditory CPT: 3.39 mm (TD) vs 3.84 mm (ADHD); passive viewing 3.63 vs 4.16 mm. Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No. Luminance confounds limit field use. Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Interpreted as LC-NE arousal and cognitive effort/attention. The HCI literature also uses pupil size for affective processing and stress, so the attention/emotion boundary is ambiguous. In healthy adults, task-evoked (not baseline) pupil tracks the vigilance decrement. Sources: Shirama et al., PLOS ONE 2020 (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0244662); Sci Rep 2026 (nature.com/articles/s41598-026-56036-0); vigilance pupillometry, Eur J Neurosci 2022 (doi 10.1111/ejn.15585); HCI pupillometry primer (arxiv.org/pdf/1608.08807)

Signal Actigraphy / fidgeting. ADHD vs neurotypical: ADHD is objectively more active (63 studies, >1,800 participants with ADHD). Strongest under high executive/working-memory demand in low-stimulation settings; minimal under low cognitive load. Similar across presentations. Strength/consistency: Strong and consistent (low heterogeneity in the De Crescenzo sleep/activity meta-analysis). Ranges: Overall d ≈ 0.36 at low cognitive load and 0.50 during in-class schoolwork. Actigraph-measured effect d = 1.30; best-case working-memory tasks d = 1.47. Actigraphy d = 0.64 vs infrared motion d = 0.92 (Murillo et al.). Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No as a trigger. Used as an assessment and treatment-monitoring aid (motion tracking in QbTest). Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Mostly physical/motor state. Kofler et al. argue movement may be *functional*, compensating for under-arousal during cognitive demand. That makes movement partly an attention/arousal signal, and "fidget = distracted" is not a safe inference. Sources: Kofler et al. 2016 meta-analysis (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4902796); De Crescenzo et al., Sleep Med Rev 2016 (sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1087079215000684); Murillo et al. 2015 (sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0165027015000837)

Signal Keystroke dynamics. ADHD vs neurotypical: No peer-reviewed ADHD-vs-NT validation found. Evidence exists only for other conditions (Parkinson's, MS, MCI) and induced psychomotor impairment. A ResearchGate preprint on "attention drift" is not peer-reviewed. Strength/consistency: Absent for ADHD. Ranges: Sleep-inertia impairment detected from key-hold times with AUC 0.93/0.91 (n = 14 healthy). Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No. Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Literature reads keystrokes as fine-motor / psychomotor state (fatigue). Mapping keystrokes to emotion is contested: typing speed, latency and duration are "only weakly correlated to emotional changes." Sources: Giancardo et al. 2015 (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25882641); keystroke meta-analysis, Sci Rep 2022 (nature.com/articles/s41598-022-11865-7); stress review (arxiv.org/pdf/1903.08511)

Signal EEG theta/beta ratio (TBR). ADHD vs neurotypical: Early studies showed elevated TBR, but the group difference shrank over time as control-group TBR rose. A 2024–2025 subtyping meta-analysis and a multiverse analysis found no diagnostic value. Strength/consistency: Null/contradictory. The classic example of an ADHD marker that failed to replicate. Ranges: Arns 2013: 9 studies, 1,253 ADHD vs 517 non-ADHD (Cz, eyes open). Canonical bands: theta 4–8 Hz, beta 13–30 Hz. Validated for real-time adaptive intervention: No. TBR neurofeedback exists but is not validated for real-time adaptation. Construct interpretation (attention vs emotion): Elevated theta has been linked to drowsiness/fatigue (physical state) and low beta to reduced concentration, so the signal confounds arousal with attention. Sources: Arns, Conners & Kraemer, J Atten Disord 2013 (doi 10.1177/1087054712460087); Boxum et al., Appl Psychophysiol Biofeedback (cris.maastrichtuniversity.nl record); multiverse analysis (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13349384)

Simulator parameter Vigilance decrement / time-on-task decay: 47-study meta-analysis: large overall CPT deficit, but only small to moderate effects for performance *over time*. Deficits reflect lower perceptual sensitivity (d′) and slower drift rate (v). By presentation: Children only; not split by presentation. Caveats: The authors attribute the small time-on-task effects partly to "easily differentiated" stimuli. Few studies reported time-binned data. Recommend: overall offset large, decay slope only modestly steeper than NT. Source: Huang-Pollock et al., J Abnorm Psychol 2012 (doi 10.1037/a0027205; pure.psu.edu record)

Simulator parameter Fatigue accumulation: No ADHD-specific fatigue-curve parameters found. In healthy adults, task-evoked pupil response and performance decline together with time on task, and EDA arousal in ADHD fluctuates more toward the end of long sessions. By presentation: Not available. Caveats: Treat as an assumption; calibrate to NT vigilance data. Source: Eur J Neurosci 2022 (doi 10.1111/ejn.15585); Psychiatry Res 2018 (S0165178118312381)

Simulator parameter Omission / commission errors: Raw rates are not pooled in sources opened. Adult meta-analysis (cited in Shirama 2020): medium–large effect for omissions (inattention) and small–medium for commissions (impulsivity). CPT diagnostic AUC 0.7–0.8 across 19 studies (secondary report). By presentation: Model omissions highest in inattentive and combined presentations, commissions in hyperactive-impulsive and combined. This split is inferred from construct mapping, not a pooled estimate. Caveats: Error rates depend heavily on target frequency (10–25% typical). Source: Shirama et al. 2020 (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0244662); Springer 2014 CPT history (doi 10.1007/s40474-014-0035-1)

Simulator parameter Intra-individual variability (IIV): RT variability vs TD: g = 0.76 (children/adolescents) and g = 0.46 (adults). Stimulants reduce it (g = −0.74). Mean RT is not slower once variability is accounted for. Minimal difference from clinical controls (g = 0.25 in children). By presentation: Reported as elevated similarly across subtypes. Caveats: Non-specific: it also characterises other disorders. Simulate IIV in NT agents too, at a lower level. Source: Kofler et al., Clin Psychol Rev 2013 (doi 10.1016/j.cpr.2013.06.001; repository.lib.fsu.edu)

Simulator parameter Response to breaks / prompts / incentives: EDA hypo-arousal normalised under fast-incentive conditions. Reinforcement improves performance in both ADHD and controls, somewhat more in ADHD. In HeartSteps (non-ADHD), suggestions initially raised steps by 66% (167 steps); the walking-suggestion effect "diminished linearly over time at 2% per day (e^b = .98)" and was indistinguishable from zero by day 28 (Klasnja et al. 2019). By presentation: Not split. Caveats: No ADHD-specific break-effect parameter found. Source: Psychiatry Res 2018; Luman et al. 2005 (doi 10.1016/j.cpr.2004.11.001); Klasnja et al., Ann Behav Med 2019 (doi 10.1093/abm/kay067)

Simulator parameter Notification acceptance / habituation: Mishra/Künzler et al. 2021: overall prompt response 70.39%. Under random timing, receptivity declined over time; ML-timed delivery gave +38% relative just-in-time response, and adaptive timing was >51% above control by day 21. EMA compliance fell from 88.9% to 70% over 14 weeks (76.5% overall). By presentation: No ADHD-specific data found. Caveats: Non-ADHD samples. The ADHD decline is plausibly steeper given delay aversion, but this is unverified and should be a sensitivity parameter. Source: Mishra et al., Proc ACM IMWUT 2021 (doi 10.1145/3463492); Howard & Lamb, Assessment 2024 (doi 10.1177/10731911231159937)

Simulator parameter Hyperactivity level (motion): Actigraph d = 1.30; working-memory tasks in low-stimulation settings d = 1.47; low cognitive load d ≈ 0.36. By presentation: Similar across inattentive and combined presentations. Caveats: Context-dependent: make motion a function of cognitive load. Source: Kofler et al. 2016 (PMC4902796)

Existing digital ADHD tool EndeavorRx (AKL-T01), Akili (Treatment claim (Rx)). Regulatory status: FDA De Novo DEN200026, Class II, 21 CFR 882.5803, product code QFT. Received 16 Apr 2020; authorised June 2020 (date from press/news coverage). Claim: "indicated to improve attention function as measured by computer-based testing in children ages 8-12 years old with primarily inattentive or combined-type ADHD… may not display benefits in typical behavioral symptoms, such as hyperactivity." Prescription only; "not intended to be used as a stand-alone therapeutic device." Evidence: STARS-ADHD RCT (Kollins et al., Lancet Digit Health 2020; n = 348; 180 vs 168). Primary endpoint TOVA API change 0.93 vs 0.03 for control (p = 0.006). 4.3% treatment-related AEs, none serious. Five studies, >600 children. Physiological sensing: No. Inputs are accelerometer tilt for steering and touch for targeting. Difficulty adapts to performance, not physiology. Verification: Yes (FDA decision summary opened)

Existing digital ADHD tool EndeavorOTC (adult) (Treatment claim (OTC)). Regulatory status: FDA 510(k) clearance, announced in Akili's press release filed as Exhibit 99.1 to its SEC Form 8-K, 18 June 2024: "EndeavorOTC was reviewed and cleared through FDA's 510(k) pathway." (A secondary news site gives 14 June 2024.) Claim: Not verified. Evidence: "The clinical study supporting EndeavorOTC's FDA clearance involved 221 adults" (Akili 8-K; a secondary site reports 223 for STARS-ADULT, NCT05183919); 45.8% met a clinically meaningful quality-of-life threshold. Physiological sensing: No Verification: Yes for 510(k) status (SEC 8-K exhibit); claim wording not verified

text: Existing digital ADHD tool Monarch eTNS, NeuroSigma (Treatment claim (Rx device)). Regulatory status: FDA De Novo DEN180041, authorised 19 April 2019. CE mark Nov 2015 (trade-press report). Claim: Treatment of ADHD in patients aged 7–12 not taking prescription ADHD medication. Evidence: 62-patient sham-controlled trial (McGough et al. 2019). Average score fell from 34.1 to 23.4 with eTNS vs 33.7 to 27.5 with sham, over 4 weeks. Physiological sensing: No sensing. Delivers nightly electrical stimulation (not adaptive). Verification: FDA De Novo yes (FDA document indexed); CE mark verified: false (secondary)

text: Existing digital ADHD tool QbTest / QbCheck, Qbtech (Assessment aid, not treatment). Regulatory status: FDA 510(k) K133382 (2014). QbCheck K190726 (secondary). CE/MDR marked (manufacturer). Claim: Aid in assessment of ADHD and evaluation of treatment interventions; results "should be interpreted only by qualified professionals." Evidence: CPT + infrared motion tracking; intended use based on 7 published studies and a registry study. Physiological sensing: Yes: motion tracking (activity), but not for real-time intervention. Verification: K133382 yes (FDA K173915 document); K190726 verified: false

Claim: Aid in assessment of attention deficits including ADHD and evaluation of treatment. Evidence: Used as the EndeavorRx primary endpoint. Physiological sensing: No Verification: Yes (FDA document)

Existing digital ADHD tool NEBA (EEG TBR) (Assessment aid). Regulatory status: FDA de novo K112711, Class II, letter dated 15 July 2013. Claim: "uses the theta/beta ratio of the EEG measured at electrode CZ on a patient 6-17 years of age combined with a clinician's evaluation to aid in the diagnosis of ADHD." Evidence: Relies on TBR, whose diagnostic value later meta-analyses dispute. Physiological sensing: Yes (EEG) Verification: Yes (FDA de novo K112711 record)
